title: Vivid thread recall — PRD notebook
content:
Purpose / elevator: quick, user-friendly way to let an assistant 'rewind' into an earlier part of a multi-turn session and surface high-signal turns as anchors so future generations can use them without always re-sending full context. Goal: improve helpfulness for long sessions while bounding cost and latency.

Background/context:
- We see two common pain points with long conversations: (1) user repeats facts to re-ground the assistant; (2) assistant loses thread (repeats or asks clarifying q's unnecessarily).
- Current options: full session replay (expensive), summary embeddings (lossy), manual + user copy-paste. Need a middle ground: compact, precise "anchors" that are cheap to store/send.

High-level idea: "Vivid Thread Recall" (VTR)
- When a turn is marked as high-signal (heuristic + user flag + eval triggers), we extract a small anchor: 1–3 short sentences, canonicalized slot form + provenance pointer.
- Anchors are stored as lightweight entries in a per-session store (KV) with metadata: token cost, timestamp, turn-id, confidence score, redaction tags.
- At model request time, a small prefetcher retrieves N anchors based on recency, importance, and cost budget and composes an auxiliary prompt segment: "Recall anchors relevant to current prompt:" followed by the anchors. Models can be taught to treat them as memory hints rather than fresh conversation.

Key properties / constraints:
- Compact: anchor payload should be < 200 tokens on average. Prefer plain text + short json-like slot string (but avoid heavy parsing server-side).
- Boundable cost: per-request anchor budget (token cap / slot cap) configurable per route/customer.
- Safe: redaction metadata must be respected; anchors flagged PII must be excluded or hashed.
- Fast: retrieval + composition should be < 10–20ms add-on to typical path for hosted API.
- Explainable: returned responses should surface which anchors were used (for diagnostics).

Who benefits:
- Product engineers building chat agents with longer sessions (support agents, tutoring, design assistants).
- Customers that need to trade off latency/cost for higher quality in long-lived sessions.

User stories (examples):
- As an end user, I want the assistant to remember the key decision I made earlier in the convo so it doesn't ask again.
- As a developer, I want to mark a turn as an anchor programmatically when an important commit or decision happens.
- As SRE, I want to enforce a per-route anchor token budget so tenants can't amplify cost.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- API: new flag on send-turn: anchor=true|false, plus optional short summary field.
- Storage: per-session anchor store implemented for Hosted API; retention TTL config per customer (default 1 day, enterprise up to 90d).
- Retrieval: server-side policy selects up to 3 anchors by score+recency under a default token cap of 150 tokens.
- Behavior: model prompt segment appended with anchors and a special delimiter; experiments show >8% reduction in repeated clarifying q's on eval dataset for 8k+ sessions.
- Observability: per-request anchor usage logged and surfaced in console (count, tokens, chosen anchors ids).

Open design questions / tradeoffs: 
- Anchor format: natural language sentence vs slotified key-value. Which generalizes better across models?
- Who computes anchor importance score? (client, server heuristics, or model-in-the-loop).
- Where to store anchors for Private deployments? Local KV vs central control plane?
- Privacy/compliance: need KMS/HSM handling if anchors contain regulated PII and retention >0.

Implementation sketch (rough):
1) Producer: SDK adds optional anchor=true and short_summary to calls (or UI allows user 'pin' action). Server receives, runs light normalization (truncate, redact patterns), computes quick heuristic score (term frequency x recency), stores anchor as record: anchor_id, session_id, text, score, tokens, timestamp, redaction_flags.
2) Retriever: on each generate request, call anchor-selector which: fetches recent anchors, filters by redaction + TTL, sorts by score, stops when token_budget reached, returns chosen anchors.
3) Composer: builds an anchors section like: "---BEGIN_ANCHORS (N)---\n[anchor-1] Purchase preference: prefers monthly billing. provenance: turn_23.\n[anchor-2] API key rotated on 2026-02-02.\n---END_ANCHORS---" and injects before user prompt.
4) Model behavior: we will ship a few prompt examples + eval harness to teach models to treat anchors as memory hints (precedence rules, do not hallucinate provenance).

API notes (proposed):
- POST /v1/sessions/{id}/turns -> body { input:..., anchor: true|false, anchor_summary: "..." }
- GET /v1/sessions/{id}/anchors?budget_tokens=150 -> list of anchor objects (id, text, tokens, score, ts)
- Route config: anchors_enabled, default_budget_tokens, retention_days, redact_level 

Privacy & redaction: 
- Default behaviour: server redacts emails/SSNs automatically using pattern heuristics and replaces with [REDACTED]. Customers can opt into PII-preserving anchor storage with explicit compliance agreements.
- Audit logs for anchor read/write actions (who retrieved anchor X).

Rollout plan / experiments:
Phase 0: internal prototype (harriet + mika) run on 1000 synthetic sessions; objective: measure retrieval latency and average anchor token size.
Phase 1: 10% of hosted-sandbox traffic with opt-in route flag; simple heuristics for anchor creation. Collect metrics: repeat-clarify-rate, latency delta, per-request token delta, cost delta.
Phase 2: expose anchor API to selected customers (GTM pairing), add retention config, refine scoring.
Phase 3: support dedicated/private: local anchor store + connector for control plane policies.

Metrics to track:
- % of sessions with anchors created
- Avg anchor tokens per session
- Mean retrieval latency (ms)
- Reduction in repeated clarifying questions (eval metric)
- Customer perceived accuracy (NPS slice)
- Cost delta / 10k tokens served

Risks / mitigations:
- Hallucination from anchors (models overfit to noisy anchors). Mitigate: anchor quality thresholds + human-in-loop review + eval gates.
- PII leakage: enforce redaction, opt-in for long retention.
- Performance regressions: start with low default budget, instrument strongly.

TODOs (near-term):
- [ ] Prototype in python SDK: anchor flag + local store mock (harriet)
- [ ] Quick eval harness to measure clarify-repeat reduction on production traces (mika)
- [ ] Draft API swagger + route config (ravi)
- [ ] Create small demo for support team to test in live sessions

Notes-to-self / loose thoughts:
- Could combine with prefix caching idea — anchors are essentially hot prefix snippets. Might reuse caching infra.
- Think about a simple UI: pin icon on message -> prompt to write 1–2 line anchor (or auto-generate).
- Might want a decay function: anchor score *= e^{-age/tau} to prefer recent facts.
- Edge case: anchors that conflict; need dedup/merge heuristics same-turn and cross-turn.

Links / references:
- thread-condensation-lab-notes (internal) — heavy overlap on condensation strategies
- session-eviction-playbook-notes — relevant for TTL decisions

Bottom line: worth prototyping. Expect small infra lift and useful win for long-form convo UX.

End of notebook.
short_description: Draft scratchpad PRD for a compact per-session anchor/rewind feature to improve long-conversation continuity while controlling cost and latency.
